headline: High: Windsurf’s shared filesystem, clipboard, MCP, and broad egress create default pathways for prompt injection, leakage, and unsafe action chaining with the non-runnable awesome-nlp profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, use clipboard, and call MCP servers, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable open-source list with no isolation or I/O surfaces. A direct injection path is not documented, but if content from shared files or clipboard is treated as instructions, the pair can be hijacked. The pathway is plausible, not proven.
conditions: IF the operator copies attacker-controlled text from a file into Windsurf or an MCP-fed workflow
IF Windsurf parses workspace content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for untrusted text
Restrict MCP servers to allowlisted, trusted endpoints
Mark external content as data-only in prompts
Use a separate workspace for untrusted files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files and has broad network egress, so sensitive file contents can leave the machine through model proxy or MCP calls. awesome-nlp itself has no data surfaces, but pairing it with Windsurf creates a default leakage path from shared files to a third party. The risk is workspace-level rather than universal, but it exists in normal use.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or open files are placed in Windsurf’s workspace
IF Windsurf sends file contents to its model proxy or an MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Disable or restrict network egress for sensitive projects
Use redacted sample files for agent-assisted work
Review MCP server permissions before enabling them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or execution capabilities, but Windsurf can write files, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses. Because Windsurf’s shared state is via local filesystem, concurrent instances can conflict on the same workspace. The conflict is one-sided in practice, yet the overlapping mutable surface is enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF two Windsurf instances operate on the same local workspace
IF one instance auto-executes commands while another edits the same git state
mitigations: Open only one Windsurf session per workspace
Turn off auto-execute for shared repos
Use separate branches per agent session
Commit or stash before switching instances

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can act on generated output via shell, git, and filesystem writes, while awesome-nlp provides no verification or execution guardrails. If Windsurf treats content derived from awesome-nlp-style outputs as authoritative, it can commit or run incorrect actions. Because downstream actions can be irreversible and the pair lacks built-in verification, high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses unverified text from the other agent as a basis for shell commands or git commits
IF auto-execute is enabled for commands derived from prior outputs
mitigations: Require human review before execution or commit
Add a verification step before any generated command is run
Disable auto-execute in Cascade
Use dry-run mode for generated changes

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, and Windsurf’s profile only shows source code/open files plus model-provider keys. The pair therefore has no clear compliance breach on the provided evidence, though Windsurf’s broad egress and workspace handling mean gaps could appear if regulated data is introduced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into Windsurf’s workspace
IF the operator routes that data to a non-compliant external model or MCP server
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a compliant deployment for sensitive projects
Audit retention settings for connected services
Document data-handling boundaries for the pair
